chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated to me from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who is affected by janabah while he is in an open desert, and he has only one garment, and semen has affected his garment, he عليه السلام said: "He performs tayammum, removes his garment, sits with himself drawn together, then performs salat (prayer) and gestures by indication."
And this report does not contradict.

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: by gesturing instead of full bodily movements
key_terms.ثَوْبٌ وَاحِدٌ: a single garment with no alternative clothing available
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen causing ritual impurity on the garment
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl
key_terms.يَطْرَحُ ثَوْبَهُ: he removes or sets aside his garment

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if his only garment is impure and he is alone in the desert?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for someone in janabah who is in the open land, lacks usable clothing, and has impurity on his only garment. It instructs him to perform tayammum and pray in a concealed seated manner with gestured movements, showing the flexibility of ritual law in cases of necessity.
